intro: Last month your manager asked you, 'Can you lead the client meeting?', told you, 'Don't be late,' and later admitted, 'I forgot to book the room.' How do you tell a friend about it now? In B1 you reported statements with said and told. Now you'll report questions, requests and orders, use verbs like suggest, warn, admit and deny with the right pattern, and learn when the tense really has to move back.
teachingNotes: Builds on b1-reported-speech-intro: say vs tell (told + person; 'She told that she was tired' ✗ → 'She said that…' / 'She told me that…'), backshift am/is → was, present simple → past simple, will → would, can → could, past simple → had + past participle, and pronoun / time / place changes (today → that day, tomorrow → the next day, here → there). Recap that in one line; don't re-teach it. New here: the full backshift list, when backshift is optional, reported questions, reported orders and requests, and reporting verbs with their patterns.

Full backshift: present continuous → past continuous (is working → was working), present perfect → past perfect (have sent → had sent), past simple → past perfect (often kept in speech: accept it), past perfect stays, past continuous usually stays, may → might, must → had to (must can also stay), would / could / should / might never change. Extra time words: this week → that week, next month → the following month, last week → the week before, ago → before. Indonesian 'sedang' and 'sudah' never change (Dia bilang dia sedang kerja dari rumah), so learners keep is working / has sent.

Backshift is optional when the reporting verb is in the present (She says she has missed the train), when the content is still true (He said the MRT doesn't / didn't run after midnight: both fine), or when you report soon after and it's still the case. With said/told, backshifting is always safe; with says it's wrong. In questions, test the optional case only with a present reporting verb, and every other question says the report is LATER and the situation is OVER, so backshift is the only right answer. Accept both forms for still-true facts.

Reported questions: same statement order as b1-indirect-questions-tags (subject before verb, no do/does/did) plus backshift. Wh-questions keep the question word: 'Where do you live?' → She asked (me) where I lived. Yes/no questions → if / whether (= apakah). No question mark. ask takes the person directly (asked me, not asked to me); 'wanted to know' works too. Common errors: 'She asked me where do I live' → 'where I lived'; 'He asked me what did I study' → 'what I had studied / studied'; 'asked me was I free' → 'asked me if I was free'. If asked: subject questions keep their order (Who called? → She asked who had called); don't raise it.

Orders and requests: tell + person + to + verb for orders and instructions, ask + person + to + verb for requests (Please… / Could you…?); negative = not to (told us not to park there). Errors from Indonesian 'jangan': 'told me don't be late', 'told me to don't be late' → 'told me not to be late'. A person must follow tell/ask here. For 'Could you…?' requests, 'asked me if I could…' is also correct: accept it unless the item asks for the 'asked me to' pattern. 'to not park' is heard in casual speech; teach 'not to'.

Reporting verbs (learn each with its pattern; there's no meaning rule): offer / refuse / promise / agree + to (offered to help, not 'offered me to help'); warn / remind / advise + person + (not) to; deny / admit + -ing (admit to + -ing and having + past participle are fine too); apologise for + -ing (US apologize); suggest + -ing or suggest (that) + person + (should) + base form. Main error, from 'menyarankan saya untuk': 'He suggested me to take a break' → 'He suggested taking a break / suggested (that) I take / I should take a break' (British also 'that I took'). Accept these that-clauses but don't test the verb form after suggest that. promise / admit / deny also take that + backshift (promised she would call). Out of scope: accuse of, insist on, blame for (only if asked), third conditional, past modals (must have), wish, causatives.

keyPoints.title: Reported questions, orders and requests
keyPoints.explanation: A reported question uses statement order, like an indirect question: subject before verb, no do/does/did, plus backshift. Yes/no questions use if or whether. Orders use tell + person + (not) to + verb; requests use ask + person + (not) to + verb.

examples.en: She asked me where I lived.
examples.id: 'Where do you live?' → Dia tanya di mana aku tinggal.

examples.en: He asked if we were ready.
examples.id: 'Are you ready?' → Dia tanya apakah kami sudah siap.

examples.en: He told me to wait outside.
examples.id: 'Wait outside.' → Dia menyuruhku menunggu di luar.

id.title: Melaporkan pertanyaan, perintah dan permintaan
id.explanation: Pertanyaan yang dilaporkan memakai susunan kalimat biasa, seperti indirect question: subjek sebelum kata kerja, tanpa do/does/did, plus backshift. Pertanyaan ya/tidak memakai if atau whether (= apakah). Perintah memakai tell + orang + (not) to + kata kerja; permintaan memakai ask + orang + (not) to + kata kerja.

keyPoints.title: Reporting verbs and their patterns
keyPoints.explanation: Verbs like suggest, warn, deny, admit and promise say what kind of thing someone said. Each has its own pattern: offer / refuse / promise + to; warn / remind + person + (not) to; deny / admit + -ing; apologise for + -ing; suggest + -ing or suggest (that) someone (should) do. Never 'suggested me to'.

examples.id: 'Let's take a taxi.' → Dia menyarankan naik taksi.

examples.en: She warned us not to touch the wires.
examples.id: 'Don't touch the wires!' → Dia memperingatkan kami agar tidak menyentuh kabelnya.
'I didn't use your laptop.' → Dia menyangkal memakai laptopku.

id.title: Reporting verbs dan polanya
id.explanation: Kata kerja seperti suggest, warn, deny, admit dan promise menunjukkan jenis ucapannya (menyarankan, memperingatkan, menyangkal, mengaku, berjanji). Masing-masing punya pola sendiri: offer / refuse / promise + to; warn / remind + orang + (not) to; deny / admit + -ing; apologise for + -ing; suggest + -ing atau suggest (that) seseorang (should) + kata kerja. Jangan pernah 'suggested me to'.

keyPoints.title: Full backshift, and when it's optional
keyPoints.explanation: Reported later, every tense moves one step back: is working → was working, has sent → had sent, sent → had sent, may → might, must → had to. had sent, would, could, should and might stay. You can keep the tense when the reporting verb is in the present (says), or when the content is still true.

examples.en: She said she was working from home.
examples.id: 'I'm working from home.' (is working → was working)

examples.en: He said he had sent the file.
examples.id: 'I've sent the file.' (has sent → had sent)

examples.en: Sari says she has missed the bus.
examples.id: Sari sekarang: 'I've missed the bus.' (says → tidak berubah)

id.title: Backshift lengkap, dan kapan boleh tidak
id.explanation: Kalau dilaporkan belakangan, setiap tense mundur satu langkah: is working → was working, has sent → had sent, sent → had sent, may → might, must → had to. had sent, would, could, should dan might tetap. Tense boleh tidak diubah kalau kata kerja pelapornya bentuk sekarang (says), atau kalau isinya masih benar.

guidedPractice.prompt: Last week a tourist at Gambir station asked you: 'Where can I buy a ticket?' Complete: She asked me where she ___ a ticket.
guidedPractice.hint: Statement order (she + verb), and can moves back to could.

guidedPractice.prompt: Yesterday Bu Ani asked Budi: 'Are you free on Saturday?' Saturday has passed. Complete with one word: Bu Ani asked Budi ___ he was free on Saturday.
guidedPractice.hint: A yes/no question has no question word, so add if or whether (= apakah).

guidedPractice.prompt: Last month the doctor said to Pak Hasan: 'Don't eat too much salt.' Complete: The doctor warned Pak Hasan ___ too much salt.
Last month Pak Hasan said: 'The team is preparing the launch.' The launch was two weeks ago. Complete: Pak Hasan said the team ___ the launch.

independentPractice.prompt: Yesterday Dimas said to the team: 'Sorry I was late.' Complete with one word: Dimas apologised for ___ late.
Last week Sari said to you: 'Remember to bring your laptop tomorrow.' Complete: Sari reminded me ___ my laptop the next day.
This morning the receptionist said to you: 'Please wait in the lobby.' Complete: She asked me ___ in the lobby.
independentPractice.hint: A request: ask + person + to + verb.

assessment.prompt: This sentence has a mistake. Write it correctly: The interviewer asked me what did I study at university.
acceptableAnswers: the interviewer asked me what i had studied at university
the interviewer asked me what i'd studied at university
the interviewer asked me what id studied at university
the interviewer asked me what i studied at university
assessment.rubric: Correct: The interviewer asked me what I had studied (or what I studied) at university: statement order (I + verb) and no did. 'what I study' = 60 (order fixed, but the interview is over, so the tense should move back). 'what had I studied' = 40 (still question order). Rewriting the sentence unchanged = 0.

assessment.prompt: Last Monday Pak Hasan asked you: 'Have you finished the sales report?' You sent it to him on Tuesday. Report his question in one English sentence. Start with: Pak Hasan asked me
acceptableAnswers: pak hasan asked me if i had finished the sales report
pak hasan asked me whether i had finished the sales report
pak hasan asked me if i'd finished the sales report
pak hasan asked me whether i'd finished the sales report
pak hasan asked me if id finished the sales report
pak hasan asked me whether id finished the sales report
assessment.rubric: Correct: Pak Hasan asked me if/whether I had finished the sales report (yes/no question → if/whether; statement order; have finished → had finished; you → I). 'the report' instead of 'the sales report' is fine. 'if I have finished' = 60 (no backshift). 'had I finished' or 'if had I finished' = 40 (question order). No if/whether ('asked me had I finished') = 30.

assessment.prompt: Last month a client, Bu Ani, said to you: 'Could you send me the invoice by Friday?' Report her request with 'asked me to'. Start with: Bu Ani asked me
acceptableAnswers: bu ani asked me to send her the invoice by friday
bu ani asked me to send the invoice to her by friday
bu ani asked me to send her the invoice by that friday
bu ani asked me to send the invoice to her by that friday
assessment.rubric: Correct: Bu Ani asked me to send her the invoice by Friday (ask + person + to + verb; me → her). 'send me the invoice' = 50 (the pronoun must change: the invoice goes to her). 'asked me if I could send her the invoice by Friday' = 70 (a correct report, but not the pattern asked for). 'asked me could I send' = 30 (question order). 'asked me send' (no to) = 40.

assessment.prompt: This sentence has a mistake. Write it correctly, keeping the verb suggested: My manager suggested me to take a day off.
acceptableAnswers: my manager suggested taking a day off
my manager suggested that i take a day off
my manager suggested i take a day off
my manager suggested that i should take a day off
my manager suggested i should take a day off
my manager suggested that i took a day off
my manager suggested i took a day off
my manager suggested my taking a day off
assessment.rubric: Correct: suggested taking a day off, or suggested (that) I (should) take a day off (British English also: that I took). 'suggested to take' = 30 (suggest is never followed by to + verb). 'suggested me taking' = 50. 'advised me to take' = 60 (correct English, but the instruction was to keep suggested). Rewriting the sentence unchanged = 0.

assessment.prompt: Last week Dimas finally said: 'OK, it was me. I broke the printer.' Complete with a form of the verb admit: Dimas ___ the printer.
acceptableAnswers: admitted breaking
admitted to breaking
admitted having broken
admitted to having broken
admitted that he had broken
admitted he had broken
admitted that he broke
admitted he broke
assessment.rubric: Correct: admitted breaking (also: admitted to breaking, admitted having broken, admitted (that) he had broken). 'admitted to break' = 30 (admit is followed by -ing or a that-clause, not to + verb). 'admitted break' or 'admitted broke' = 20. 'admits breaking' = 70 (right pattern, but it happened last week).

assessment.prompt: Last year Pak Hasan said: 'I've never been to Japan.' In March he finally visited Tokyo. Complete with one word: Pak Hasan said he ___ never been to Japan.
acceptableAnswers: had
assessment.rubric: Correct: had (have been → had been: the present perfect moves back to the past perfect). 'has' = 20 (it's no longer true: he has been to Japan now). 'was' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Last month, on a work trip in Surabaya, Dimas told you: 'I'm meeting a client here tomorrow.' Now you're back in Jakarta and tell a colleague. Report it in one English sentence. Start with: Dimas told me
acceptableAnswers: dimas told me he was meeting a client there the next day
dimas told me that he was meeting a client there the next day
dimas told me he was meeting a client there the following day
dimas told me that he was meeting a client there the following day
assessment.rubric: Correct: Dimas told me (that) he was meeting a client there the next day / the following day (am meeting → was meeting; here → there; tomorrow → the next day). Each part missed costs about 30: 'is meeting', 'here', 'tomorrow'. 'in Surabaya' instead of 'there' is fine. 'I was meeting' = 40 (the pronoun must change to he).

blocks.text:
Quick recap from B1: when you report **later**, use **said** (no person after it) or **told** + person, and move the verb **one step back** into the past (**backshift**): *am → was*, *work → worked*, *will → would*, *can → could*, *went → had gone*. People, time and place change to your point of view: *I → she*, *tomorrow → the next day*, *here → there*.

At B2 you need **every** tense:
- **present continuous → past continuous**: *'I'm working from home.'* → *She said she **was working** from home.*
- **present perfect → past perfect**: *'I've sent the file.'* → *He said he **had sent** the file.*
- **past simple → past perfect**: *'I sent it.'* → *He said he **had sent** it.* (In everyday speech the past simple often stays: *he said he sent it*.)
- **past perfect stays**: it can't go further back. **Past continuous** usually stays too: *'I was driving.'* → *He said he **was driving**.*
- **may → might**, **must → had to** (*must* can also stay).
- **would, could, should, might** never change.

More time words: **this week → that week**, **next month → the following month**, **last week → the week before**, **two days ago → two days before**.

id.text:
Ulasan singkat dari B1: kalau kamu melapor **belakangan**, pakai **said** (tidak diikuti orang) atau **told** + orang, lalu mundurkan kata kerjanya **satu langkah** ke masa lampau (**backshift**): *am → was*, *work → worked*, *will → would*, *can → could*, *went → had gone*. Orang, waktu dan tempat berubah ke sudut pandangmu: *I → she*, *tomorrow → the next day*, *here → there*.

Di B2 kamu perlu **semua** tense:
- **present continuous → past continuous**: *'I'm working from home.'* → *She said she **was working** from home.*
- **present perfect → past perfect**: *'I've sent the file.'* → *He said he **had sent** the file.*
- **past simple → past perfect**: *'I sent it.'* → *He said he **had sent** it.* (Dalam percakapan sehari-hari past simple sering dibiarkan: *he said he sent it*.)
- **past perfect tetap**: tidak bisa mundur lebih jauh lagi. **Past continuous** biasanya juga tetap: *'I was driving.'* → *He said he **was driving**.*
- **may → might**, **must → had to** (*must* juga boleh tetap).
- **would, could, should, might** tidak pernah berubah.

Keterangan waktu lainnya: **this week → that week** (minggu itu), **next month → the following month** (bulan berikutnya), **last week → the week before** (seminggu sebelumnya), **two days ago → two days before** (dua hari sebelumnya).

rows.en: Sari said she was waiting for the KRL.
Budi said he had already paid the bill.
Bu Ani said the meeting might start late.
Pak Hasan said we had to finish the report that week.
rows.id: Pak Hasan: 'Kalian harus menyelesaikan laporannya minggu ini.'
rows.note: must → had to; this week → that week

id.note: must → had to; this week → that week

rows.en: Rina said she should call her mother.

blocks.text: **The sedang / sudah trap.** Indonesian keeps *sedang* and *sudah* the same whenever you report them: *Dia bilang dia **sedang** kerja dari rumah*, *Dia bilang dia **sudah** kirim filenya*. English moves them back: *sedang* (is + -ing) → **was + -ing**; *sudah* (has + past participle) → **had + past participle**. So when you see *said* and the moment is over, check the helper verb: *is → was*, *has → had*.

id.text: **Jebakan sedang / sudah.** Dalam bahasa Indonesia, *sedang* dan *sudah* tidak berubah saat dilaporkan: *Dia bilang dia **sedang** kerja dari rumah*, *Dia bilang dia **sudah** kirim filenya*. Bahasa Inggris memundurkannya: *sedang* (is + -ing) → **was + -ing**; *sudah* (has + past participle) → **had + past participle**. Jadi kalau kamu melihat *said* dan momennya sudah lewat, cek kata kerja bantunya: *is → was*, *has → had*.

blocks.prompt: Last month Bu Ani said: 'I've lost my office key.' She found it the next day. Bu Ani said she ___ her office key.
blocks.explain: She spoke a month ago and the key was found, so the present perfect moves back: **has lost → had lost**. *has lost* sounds like the key is still missing; *lost had* is the wrong order.

id.prompt: Bulan lalu Bu Ani bilang: 'I've lost my office key.' Besoknya kuncinya ketemu. Lengkapi: Bu Ani said she ___ her office key.
id.explain: Dia bicara sebulan lalu dan kuncinya sudah ketemu, jadi present perfect mundur: **has lost → had lost**. *has lost* terdengar seolah kuncinya masih hilang; *lost had* urutannya salah.

material.title: When you can keep the tense

blocks.text:
Backshift isn't always needed. You can keep the original tense when:
- **The reporting verb is in the present**: *says*, *has said*, *is telling*. You're passing on the message while it's still happening: Sari is texting you now, *'I've missed the bus.'* → *Sari **says** she **has missed** the bus.* Here backshift is **wrong**.
- **It's still true**: *'The MRT doesn't run after midnight.'* → *He said the MRT **doesn't** run after midnight* (it still doesn't). *didn't run* is also correct.
- **You report it soon after and nothing has changed**: Rina, five minutes ago: *'I'm really tired.'* → *Rina said she**'s** really tired* (she still is).

The safe rule: with **said / told**, backshift is always correct. Keeping the present is an **option** only when the content is still true now. When the situation is **over** (she isn't tired any more, the meeting has happened, *tomorrow* has passed), you **must** move the tense back.

id.text:
Backshift tidak selalu perlu. Tense aslinya boleh dipertahankan kalau:
- **Kata kerja pelapornya bentuk sekarang**: *says*, *has said*, *is telling*. Kamu menyampaikan pesan saat pesannya masih berlangsung: Sari sedang mengirim pesan kepadamu, *'I've missed the bus.'* → *Sari **says** she **has missed** the bus.* Di sini backshift justru **salah**.
- **Isinya masih benar**: *'The MRT doesn't run after midnight.'* → *He said the MRT **doesn't** run after midnight* (memang masih begitu). *didn't run* juga benar.
- **Kamu melapor tidak lama kemudian dan belum ada yang berubah**: Rina, lima menit lalu: *'I'm really tired.'* → *Rina said she**'s** really tired* (dia masih capek).

Aturan amannya: dengan **said / told**, backshift selalu benar. Mempertahankan bentuk sekarang hanyalah **pilihan**, dan hanya kalau isinya masih benar sekarang. Kalau situasinya sudah **lewat** (dia sudah tidak capek, rapatnya sudah terjadi, *besok*-nya sudah lewat), tense-nya **harus** dimundurkan.

rows.en: Dimas says he's stuck in traffic.
She said Jakarta is bigger than Bandung.
He said he was in Bali.
rows.id: Dia (bulan lalu): 'Saya di Bali.' Sekarang dia sudah pulang.

blocks.prompt: Yesterday Sari said: 'The MRT doesn't run after midnight.' This is still true. Which report is correct?
options: Sari said the MRT doesn't run after midnight.
Sari said the MRT didn't run after midnight.
blocks.explain: It's **still true**, so keeping the present is fine, and backshift (*didn't run*) is always correct after *said*. Both work.

id.prompt: Kemarin Sari bilang: 'The MRT doesn't run after midnight.' Ini masih benar. Laporan mana yang benar?
id.explain: Isinya **masih benar**, jadi bentuk sekarang boleh dipertahankan, dan backshift (*didn't run*) selalu benar setelah *said*. Keduanya benar.

blocks.text:
Remember indirect questions from B1? *Could you tell me where **the station is**?* After the opening, the question becomes a normal statement. Reported questions work the same way, plus backshift:
- Use **asked** (with or without a person: *She asked **me**…*, *She asked…*) or **wanted to know**. Not *asked to me*.
- **Question word questions**: keep the question word, then **subject + verb** (statement order). **do / does / did disappear**: *'Where **do** you live?'* → *She asked me where **I lived**.* *'What time **does** the train leave?'* → *He asked what time **the train left**.*
- **Yes/no questions** have no question word, so add **if** or **whether** (= apakah): *'Are you free on Friday?'* → *He asked **if** I **was** free on Friday.* *if* is more common; *whether* is a bit more formal.
- A reported question is a statement: it ends with a **full stop**, not a question mark.

id.text:
Ingat indirect questions dari B1? *Could you tell me where **the station is**?* Setelah kalimat pembukanya, pertanyaannya berubah jadi kalimat biasa. Pertanyaan yang dilaporkan bekerja dengan cara yang sama, ditambah backshift:
- Pakai **asked** (dengan atau tanpa orang: *She asked **me**…*, *She asked…*) atau **wanted to know** (ingin tahu). Bukan *asked to me*.
- **Pertanyaan dengan kata tanya** (where, what, why, how…): kata tanyanya tetap, lalu **subjek + kata kerja** (susunan kalimat biasa). **do / does / did hilang**: *'Where **do** you live?'* → *She asked me where **I lived**.* *'What time **does** the train leave?'* → *He asked what time **the train left**.*
- **Pertanyaan ya/tidak** tidak punya kata tanya, jadi tambahkan **if** atau **whether** (= apakah): *'Are you free on Friday?'* → *He asked **if** I **was** free on Friday.* *if* lebih umum; *whether* sedikit lebih formal.
- Pertanyaan yang dilaporkan adalah kalimat biasa: diakhiri **titik**, bukan tanda tanya.

rows.en: She asked me where I lived.
He asked what time the train left.
The officer asked why I had come to Bali.
Bu Ani asked if we were ready.
The landlord wanted to know whether I could pay in cash.

blocks.text:
**The question-order trap.** The most common mistake is keeping the question inside the report: *She asked me where **do I live*** ✗ → *where **I lived***. *He asked me **was I** free* ✗ → *if **I was** free*. Quick check: after the question word (or *if*), is the **subject** first? Is there a *do/does/did*? Then fix it.

Indonesian helps a little here: *Dia tanya aku tinggal di mana* already has *aku* before *tinggal*. Just move the question word to the front: *where I lived*.

id.text:
**Jebakan susunan pertanyaan.** Kesalahan paling umum adalah tetap memakai susunan pertanyaan di dalam laporan: *She asked me where **do I live*** ✗ → *where **I lived***. *He asked me **was I** free* ✗ → *if **I was** free*. Cek cepat: setelah kata tanya (atau *if*), apakah **subjeknya** di depan? Apakah ada *do/does/did*? Kalau ada, perbaiki.

Bahasa Indonesia sedikit membantu di sini: *Dia tanya aku tinggal di mana* sudah menaruh *aku* sebelum *tinggal*. Tinggal pindahkan kata tanyanya ke depan: *where I lived*.

blocks.prompt: Last week a recruiter asked Rina: 'How long have you worked at the bank?' The recruiter asked Rina how long ___ at the bank.
blocks.explain: Statement order: **she** (subject) before **had worked**, and *have worked* moves back to *had worked*. *had she worked* and *did she work* keep the question order.

id.prompt: Minggu lalu seorang perekrut bertanya kepada Rina: 'How long have you worked at the bank?' Lengkapi: The recruiter asked Rina how long ___ at the bank.
id.explain: Susunan kalimat biasa: **she** (subjek) sebelum **had worked**, dan *have worked* mundur jadi *had worked*. *had she worked* dan *did she work* masih memakai susunan pertanyaan.

id.title: Pertanyaan yang dilaporkan: susunan kalimat biasa

material.title: Orders and requests: tell / ask someone to

blocks.text:
Orders, instructions and requests don't need any tense change. They use a simple pattern: **verb + person + to + base verb** (the **base verb** is the basic form, like *wait, call, be*).
- **Orders and instructions → tell**: *'Wait here.'* → *He **told me to wait** there.*
- **Requests** (*Please…*, *Could you…?*) **→ ask**: *'Please call me back.'* → *She **asked me to call** her back.*
- **Negative → not to**: *'Don't be late.'* → *She told us **not to be** late.*

The person is required: *He told **me** to wait*, not *He told to wait*. For a *Could you…?* request you can also report the question itself: *She asked me **if I could** call her back.* Both are correct.

id.text:
Perintah, instruksi dan permintaan tidak perlu perubahan tense. Polanya sederhana: **kata kerja + orang + to + base verb** (**base verb** = bentuk dasar kata kerja, misalnya *wait, call, be*).
- **Perintah dan instruksi → tell**: *'Wait here.'* → *He **told me to wait** there.*
- **Permintaan** (*Please…*, *Could you…?*) **→ ask**: *'Please call me back.'* → *She **asked me to call** her back.*
- **Bentuk negatif → not to**: *'Don't be late.'* → *She told us **not to be** late.*

Orangnya wajib ada: *He told **me** to wait*, bukan *He told to wait*. Untuk permintaan *Could you…?* kamu juga boleh melaporkan pertanyaannya: *She asked me **if I could** call her back.* Keduanya benar.

rows.en: The driver told us to fasten our seatbelts.
Rina asked me to check her email.
rows.note: request → asked + person + to; my → her

id.note: permintaan → asked + orang + to; my → her

rows.en: My mother told me not to come home late.
The teacher asked the students not to use their phones.

blocks.text: **The jangan trap.** Indonesian just puts the original words in: *Dia bilang ke kami **jangan** terlambat.* So learners write *She told us **don't** be late* ✗ or *told us **to don't** be late* ✗. In English, **don't → not to**: *She told us **not to be** late.* *not* comes **before** *to*.

id.text: **Jebakan jangan.** Bahasa Indonesia tinggal memasukkan kata aslinya: *Dia bilang ke kami **jangan** terlambat.* Jadi banyak yang menulis *She told us **don't** be late* ✗ atau *told us **to don't** be late* ✗. Dalam bahasa Inggris, **don't → not to**: *She told us **not to be** late.* *not* ada **sebelum** *to*.

blocks.prompt: At dinner, Rina said to the waiter: 'Could you bring the bill, please?' Rina ___ the waiter to bring the bill.
blocks.explain: It's a polite **request**, so **ask + person + to**: *asked the waiter to bring*. *said* can't be followed by a person, and *told to the waiter* is wrong: the person comes straight after *told*.

id.prompt: Saat makan malam, Rina bilang ke pelayan: 'Could you bring the bill, please?' Lengkapi: Rina ___ the waiter to bring the bill.
id.explain: Ini **permintaan** yang sopan, jadi **ask + orang + to**: *asked the waiter to bring*. *said* tidak bisa langsung diikuti orang, dan *told to the waiter* salah: orangnya harus langsung setelah *told*.

id.title: Perintah dan permintaan: tell / ask someone to

material.title: Reporting verbs: suggest, warn, admit, deny, promise…

blocks.text:
Instead of *said* every time, a **reporting verb** tells the listener what kind of thing was said: a suggestion, a warning, a promise. Each verb has its own pattern. There's no logic to guess it, so learn each verb together with its pattern:
- **+ to + verb**: **offer, refuse, promise, agree** (from B1). *'I'll help you.'* → *He **offered to help** me* (not *offered me to help*). *'I won't sign it.'* → *She **refused to sign** it.*
- **+ person + (not) to + verb**: **warn, remind, advise** (like *tell* and *ask*). *'Don't touch the wires!'* → *She **warned us not to touch** the wires.* *'Remember to bring your ID.'* → *He **reminded me to bring** my ID.*
- **+ -ing**: **deny**, **admit**, **suggest**, and **apologise for**. *'I didn't use your laptop.'* → *He **denied using** my laptop.* *'Sorry I'm late.'* → *She **apologised for being** late.* The -ing form already shows it happened before, so you don't need *had*.
- **+ that + sentence**: **suggest, admit, deny, promise, warn**. *'I'll call you tonight.'* → *She **promised (that) she would call** me that night.* With **suggest**: *suggested (that) we (should) + base verb*: *He suggested (that) we **take / should take** a taxi.*

id.text:
Daripada *said* terus, **reporting verb** (kata kerja pelapor) memberi tahu pendengar jenis ucapannya: saran, peringatan, janji. Setiap kata kerja punya pola sendiri. Tidak ada logika untuk menebaknya, jadi hafalkan setiap kata kerja bersama polanya:
- **+ to + kata kerja**: **offer** (menawarkan diri), **refuse** (menolak), **promise** (berjanji), **agree** (setuju), dari B1. *'I'll help you.'* → *He **offered to help** me* (bukan *offered me to help*). *'I won't sign it.'* → *She **refused to sign** it.*
- **+ orang + (not) to + kata kerja**: **warn** (memperingatkan), **remind** (mengingatkan), **advise** (menasihati), seperti *tell* dan *ask*. *'Don't touch the wires!'* → *She **warned us not to touch** the wires.* *'Remember to bring your ID.'* → *He **reminded me to bring** my ID.*
- **+ -ing**: **deny** (menyangkal), **admit** (mengaku), **suggest** (menyarankan), dan **apologise for** (minta maaf karena). *'I didn't use your laptop.'* → *He **denied using** my laptop.* *'Sorry I'm late.'* → *She **apologised for being** late.* Bentuk -ing sudah menunjukkan kejadiannya lebih dulu, jadi tidak perlu *had*.
- **+ that + kalimat**: **suggest, admit, deny, promise, warn**. *'I'll call you tonight.'* → *She **promised (that) she would call** me that night.* Dengan **suggest**: *suggested (that) we (should) + base verb*: *He suggested (that) we **take / should take** a taxi.*

rows.en: Budi offered to drive us to the airport.
The guide warned us not to swim there.
Sari admitted forgetting the meeting.
Pak Hasan suggested postponing the launch.
Pak Hasan suggested that we should postpone the launch.
The company apologised for sending the wrong order.
rows.id: 'We're sorry we sent the wrong order.'

blocks.text:
**The menyarankan trap.** *Dia menyarankan saya untuk istirahat* makes people write *He suggested **me to** take a break* ✗. **suggest** never takes *person + to*. Say *He suggested **taking** a break* or *He suggested (that) **I take / I should take** a break*. (British English also says *that I took*.) If you want *person + to*, use **advise**: *He **advised me to** take a break.*

Spelling: British **apologise**, American **apologize**. And **warn** sounds like *worn* (it rhymes with *born*), not like *want*.

id.text:
**Jebakan menyarankan.** *Dia menyarankan saya untuk istirahat* membuat orang menulis *He suggested **me to** take a break* ✗. **suggest** tidak pernah diikuti *orang + to*. Katakan *He suggested **taking** a break* atau *He suggested (that) **I take / I should take** a break*. (Bahasa Inggris British juga memakai *that I took*.) Kalau mau pola *orang + to*, pakai **advise**: *He **advised me to** take a break.*

Ejaan: British **apologise**, Amerika **apologize**. Dan **warn** dibaca seperti *worn* (berima dengan *born*), bukan seperti *want*.

blocks.prompt: 'Let's meet at the café near the station,' Dimas said. Dimas suggested ___ at the café near the station.
blocks.explain: **suggest + -ing**: *suggested meeting*. *suggested to meet* and *suggested us to meet* are the classic mistakes: suggest is never followed by *to* + verb.

id.prompt: 'Let's meet at the café near the station,' kata Dimas. Lengkapi: Dimas suggested ___ at the café near the station.
id.explain: **suggest + -ing**: *suggested meeting*. *suggested to meet* dan *suggested us to meet* adalah kesalahan klasik: suggest tidak pernah diikuti *to* + kata kerja.

What's the difference between 'He told me to wait' and 'He asked me to wait'?
Why is 'He suggested me to go' wrong?
When can I keep the present tense in reported speech?

flashcards.front: 'Where do you live?' → She asked me…
flashcards.back: where I lived (no do; I + verb)
suggested taking a break / suggested (that) I (should) take a break
warned / reminded + person + (not) to (warned us not to swim)
says (present reporting verb), or it's still true

id.intro: Bulan lalu manajermu bertanya, 'Can you lead the client meeting?', bilang, 'Don't be late,' lalu belakangan mengaku, 'I forgot to book the room.' Bagaimana kamu menceritakannya ke teman sekarang? Di B1 kamu sudah melaporkan pernyataan dengan said dan told. Sekarang kamu akan melaporkan pertanyaan, permintaan dan perintah, memakai kata kerja seperti suggest, warn, admit dan deny dengan pola yang benar, dan belajar kapan tense benar-benar harus dimundurkan.
suggestedQuestions: Kenapa 'where I lived', bukan 'where did I live'?
Apa bedanya 'He told me to wait' dan 'He asked me to wait'?
Kenapa 'He suggested me to go' salah?
Kapan aku boleh tetap memakai present tense dalam reported speech?

assessment.rsb-1: Kalimat ini ada kesalahannya. Tulis kalimat yang benar: The interviewer asked me what did I study at university.
assessment.rsb-2: Senin lalu Pak Hasan bertanya kepadamu: 'Have you finished the sales report?' Kamu mengirimkannya hari Selasa. Laporkan pertanyaannya dalam satu kalimat bahasa Inggris. Mulai dengan: Pak Hasan asked me
assessment.rsb-3: Bulan lalu seorang klien, Bu Ani, bilang kepadamu: 'Could you send me the invoice by Friday?' Laporkan permintaannya dengan pola 'asked me to'. Mulai dengan: Bu Ani asked me
assessment.rsb-4: Kalimat ini ada kesalahannya. Tulis kalimat yang benar, tetap dengan kata kerja suggested: My manager suggested me to take a day off.
assessment.rsb-5: Minggu lalu Dimas akhirnya bilang: 'OK, it was me. I broke the printer.' Lengkapi dengan bentuk kata kerja admit: Dimas ___ the printer.
assessment.rsb-6: Tahun lalu Pak Hasan bilang: 'I've never been to Japan.' Bulan Maret dia akhirnya pergi ke Tokyo. Lengkapi dengan satu kata: Pak Hasan said he ___ never been to Japan.
assessment.rsb-7: Bulan lalu, saat perjalanan dinas di Surabaya, Dimas bilang kepadamu: 'I'm meeting a client here tomorrow.' Sekarang kamu sudah kembali di Jakarta dan bercerita ke rekan kerja. Laporkan ucapannya dalam satu kalimat bahasa Inggris. Mulai dengan: Dimas told me
